title: How Many? The كَمْ Rule

blocks: ## The question is plural in meaning but singular in grammar
كَمْ asks for a number, while the following counted noun identifies the category in a fixed singular accusative form.
[ar] كَمْ وَلَدًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟
[ar] كَمْ سَيَّارَةً رَأَيْتَ؟
[ar] كَمْ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا اشْتَرَيْتِ؟
[ar] كَمْ مَرَّةً تَتَدَرَّبُ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ؟
[callout] Cambridge relevance: the rule appears in practical questions about people, items, days, hours, visits and frequency, and it is easy to check accurately in writing.
## Choose your route
Secure the fixed noun form, then add spelling, modifiers and response patterns.
### Core
- Use كَمْ + singular noun.
- Make the noun indefinite accusative.
- Use common forms such as كَمْ كِتَابًا and كَمْ مَرَّةً.
### Develop
- Spell tanwīn fatḥ and its supporting alif accurately.
- Add a matching adjective.
- Distinguish counted-noun questions from fixed questions such as كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟
### Stretch
- Use كَمْ across tenses and complex sentences.
- Form natural survey and data questions.
- Edit both question and answer without mixing the two number systems.
## Starter diagnostic
Choose the noun form that follows interrogative كَمْ.
## The core formula
Treat the phrase as one dependable pattern before adding more complex number rules.
[callout] Formula: كَمْ + اِسْمٌ مُفْرَدٌ نَكِرَةٌ مَنْصُوبٌ

TABLE: Meaning | Correct question phrase | Not this // how many students | كَمْ طَالِبًا | كَمْ طُلَّابٍ // how many girls | كَمْ بِنْتًا | كَمْ بَنَاتٍ // how many schools | كَمْ مَدْرَسَةً | كَمْ مَدَارِسَ // how many days | كَمْ يَوْمًا | كَمْ أَيَّامٍ // how many times | كَمْ مَرَّةً | كَمْ مَرَّاتٍ
[callout] Memory phrase: the number is unknown, so the category noun appears once—in the singular—after كَمْ.
## Tanwīn fatḥ spelling
The accusative sound is consistent, but the written supporting alif depends on the noun ending.

TABLE: Noun type | Correct form | Spelling note // Regular consonant ending | كِتَابًا، قَلَمًا، يَوْمًا | Add the supporting alif. // Tāʾ marbūṭa | سَيَّارَةً، مَدْرَسَةً، مَرَّةً | No additional alif after ة. // Hamza after alif | مَاءً | No extra alif is added.
[callout/warning] Common visual error: سَيَّارَةًا is incorrect. The tāʾ marbūṭa already provides the written support for tanwīn fatḥ.
## Add adjectives and other modifiers
Any adjective describing the counted noun follows its singular accusative form.
[ar] كَمْ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا اشْتَرَيْتَ؟
[ar] كَمْ سَيَّارَةً سَرِيعَةً رَأَيْتِ؟
[callout] Important: the answer may use a normal number expression with different noun rules. Do not copy the question’s singular accusative form mechanically into the answer.
## High-frequency كَمْ questions
Some practical questions use a counted noun; others are fixed possession, age, price or time expressions.

TABLE: Purpose | Question | Note // Number of people/items | كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ | Core singular accusative rule // Frequency | كَمْ مَرَّةً تَتَدَرَّبُ؟ | مَرَّةً is counted // Duration | كَمْ يَوْمًا بَقِيتَ؟ | يَوْمًا is counted // Age | كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ | Fixed possession-style question; no counted noun follows immediately // Price | كَمْ ثَمَنُ هَذَا؟ / بِكَمْ هَذَا؟ | Ask the price rather than forcing a counted noun
[callout] Do not overapply one rule: the singular accusative rule governs the distinguishing counted noun after interrogative كَمْ. Fixed expressions such as كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ have their own structure.
## Answering كَمْ questions
The question tests كَمْ structure; the answer uses an appropriate number expression.
### Question
كَمْ كِتَابًا قَرَأْتَ؟
### Answer
قَرَأْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ كُتُبٍ.
The answer follows ordinary number–noun rules, not the كَمْ counted-noun form.
### Question
كَمْ مَرَّةً تَسْبَحِينَ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ؟
### Answer
أَسْبَحُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ.
The answer uses the dual frequency expression.
[callout] Speaking strategy: answer the number, then add a time, reason or comparison so the response demonstrates wider language control.
## Misconception clinic
Repair plural nouns, definiteness, case and tanwīn spelling.
## كَمْ repair game
Choose the singular accusative form and accurate spelling.
## Four-skills application
Use كَمْ to collect, understand and report quantities.
### Listening: survey totals
Listen to a partner read five كَمْ questions and answers. Record the counted category and number, then check whether the question noun was singular accusative.
### Reading: class survey
كَمْ طَالِبًا يَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟ كَمْ طَالِبَةً تَرْكَبُ الْحَافِلَةَ؟ كَمْ مَرَّةً يُمَارِسُونَ الرِّيَاضَةَ؟
Identify the category, tense and counted noun in each question.
### Speaking questionnaire
Ask about books, siblings, school subjects, weekly activities, journeys and screen time. Extend every answer.
### Data report
Convert answers into statements using ordinary number–noun patterns. Check that the answer does not simply repeat the question form.
### Create a class or family survey
Write eight كَمْ questions, collect or invent answers, then write a short report comparing the results.

[callout] Success checklist: Use eight singular accusative counted nouns, two feminine nouns, two adjectives, one duration question, one frequency question, one fixed age/price question and accurate answer-side number phrases.
## Final mastery check
Show that you can apply the singular accusative rule and recognise its limits.
### You can now
- Use كَمْ with a singular indefinite accusative counted noun.
- Spell tanwīn fatḥ with or without a supporting alif.
- Add matching singular accusative adjectives.
- Use high-frequency frequency and duration questions.
- Recognise fixed age and price questions.
- Answer with appropriate ordinary number grammar.
Spaced revisit: audit every كَمْ question in a previous worksheet or lesson and repair the counted noun form.
